To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aberrant promoter methyla-tion is a frequent and specific event in breast cancer.
epigenetic inactivating mechanisms are frequent and early events in breast cancer development and that the methylation status of specific genes may be useful as a prognostic factor.
the methylation status of the promoter region of genes is a useful biomarker for the diagnosis and prognosis of breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the epigenetic inactivations of the genes CDH1, DAPK1, DCC, GSTP1, HIC1, MGMT, p14(ARF), p15(INK4B), p16(INK4A), p73, RARbeta2, RASSF1A, RIZ1, RUNX3, SFRP1 and SFRP2.
the epigenetic regulation and the aberrant methylation status of growth-regulatory gene promoters, which are involved in the pathogenesis and progression of breast cancer.
the identification of epigenetically inactivated genes and their role as biomarkers for breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
epigenetic inactivating mechanisms are involved in the pathogenesis of human breast cancer, but the exact role of epigenetic alterations remains to be clarified.

the methylation status of several genes is associated with breast cancer development and progression and that the methylation of these genes may serve as a marker for the diagnosis and prognosis of breast cancer.

the aberrant DNA methylation pattern in breast cancer cells is a complex and heterogeneous event, which is not only a consequence of the genetic background but is also influenced by environmental factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
epigenetic inactivity is a common phenomenon in breast cancer.
the aberrant methylation pattern in breast cancer is a result of a combination of genetic and environmental factors.
epigenetic alterations in breast cancer are a frequent and early phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that

aberrant promoter methyla- tion of growth-regulatory and tumor suppressor genes is an early event in the development and progres- sion of breast cancer, but that the extent of methylation varies between the different subtypes and histological grades of breast cancer.
the aberrant methylation status of the investigated genes can serve as a prognostic marker for the development and progression in breast cancer.
epigenetic changes in the promoter region, in particular aberrant promoter methyla- tion, are a frequent event in breast cancer.
